Wyatt Cannon
for Violin
and Live Electronics
Dur: 6'
Memory Palace
For Piano and Live Electronics
Dur: 6'
Written in 2026 for Sean Smith at IU's Spring 2026 Center for
Electronic and Computer Music Concert.
Many thanks to him for the premiere performance.
Requirements
1. SuperCollider 3.
2. 8 channel audio setup. (For stereo or quad version, contact the
composer)
3. Clip on condensor microphone for violin.
4. An audio interface with 8 channel output.
5. The patch from github.com/tellmewyatt/memory-palace.
Click on the green "Code" box then "Download Zip".
6. An assistant is recommended to play the electronics part, but
this piece can also be performed completely solo with the violinist
cuing each cue with a foot pedal. The pedal should be programmed to
output spaces, if it is used.
To Play
1. Select your audio device from your system settings BEFORE starting
SuperCollider.
2. Open "main.scd" in SuperCollider. Hit "CMD+A" then "CMD+ENTER" to
run the patch. Select the score window. It should say "nil",
which means that we are at the beginning of the piece with no patch
selected.
3. Press SPACE to advance to the next cue. To start at a specific cue,
type the character marked in the electronics part to play it. Cues
that do not depend on a previous cue are marked in the score with a
square, while those that do are marked with a circle. Therefore it
will often be advisable to start at square cues during rehearsal.
Questions?
Contact the composer at composer@wyattcannon.
